notes: Nonce forms are DAX for the functional auxiliary and MIP for the lexical adjective in this draft; counterbalance nonce forms across morphosyntactic conditions in the final experiment.
Training is positive-only. Participants overhear native speakers and do not judge DAX/MIP. Occasional comprehension questions should test story details rather than the nonce word.

Root training is restricted to deontic/permission possibility for Experiment 1. Root targets are future-oriented eventives; epistemic targets use past perfect, present progressive, or present stative environments.
Include some subject-auxiliary inversion during training to establish auxiliary status. Negation is excluded because possibility modals can interact ambiguously with negation.
Critical trials make deontic and epistemic interpretations disagree. Root-to-epistemic critical trials are D-E+; epistemic-to-root critical trials are D+E-.
Critical test targets are kept syntactically conservative. Temporal-orientation cues are retained in Experiment 1 because they are part of the acquisition hypothesis.

Fillers also contain the nonce word. Half are D+E+ and half D-E-, so deontic and epistemic interpretations converge on the same response. Their purpose is to obscure the flavor manipulation, not merely to act as easy attention checks.
Vary discourse structure, information order, deontic wording, epistemic evidence, and integrated background details so that no prose template reveals which information is diagnostic.
For critical items, norm at least two contrasting discourse orders. Prefer items whose D/E interpretation is robust across orderings rather than statistically correcting a fragile item.
The first test trial should be critical so that a filler containing the nonce word in a new temporal/aspectual environment does not alter the representation before initial transfer is measured.
